source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to update the vendor's bank details whenever the invoice shows new ones, with no instruction to verify the change against an independent, pre-registered channel. Untrusted invoice content is treated as sufficient basis for a sensitive, high-impact write.

The only safety control for bank changes and payments is a prompt instruction to request approval with a one line summary. What the summary discloses is left to the model's judgment; there is no structural requirement that it include the bank account number or that a bank detail change occurred.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model's one-line summary, not the raw bank account number or change history. A more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from an upgraded model can secure approval for a fraudulent change (ASI09). High approval volume (~150 cards/day) compounds this with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of new bank details before the change takes effect
controls.decay_rationale: Verification against a pre-registered contact channel (for example a callback to the phone number on file before the invoice arrived) happens outside the model and does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Raw action approval card showing account number, prior value, and diff
controls.decay_rationale: Once the approver is shown the system-of-record values directly rather than a model-generated summary, effectiveness no longer depends on the model choosing to disclose them.

controls.name: Scope the ERP credential to the matched vendor and in-queue invoices only
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot act beyond its grant regardless of how it is manipulated.

findings.title: Summary-gated vendor bank change and payment scheduling (TC9) decays under model upgrade and approval fatigue

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice uploaded to the supplier portal; supplier portals are a classic vendor-impersonation / business email compromise vector.
Agent reads the vendor master record to match the invoice to a vendor and PO.
Agent writes new bank details taken directly from unverified invoice content (prompt.md:2).
Agent schedules an irreversible payment, which will be sent to the just-updated, potentially fraudulent bank account.
The only gate before bank_update and schedule_payment; shown to the clerk as a one-line model summary, with no account number or change history.

forecast.watch_signal: A model or platform version change with no documented re-review of the approval summary logic (subject.model.swappable is true); or clerk approvals per day rising further above the current ~150/day baseline. Either indicates the model-summary gate is decaying toward ineffectiveness.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update the vendor record whenever the invoice shows new bank details, with no instruction to verify the change against an independent channel.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The card displays only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521).' There is no bank account number, no flag that a bank detail change occurred, and no change history.
Bank account numbers and the change history are explicitly not shown to the clerk; the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; the model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review.
The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, so a successful bypass is not limited to the matched vendor or invoice amount.

recommendations.action: Require independent, out-of-band verification of any new bank details (for example a callback to a phone number on file before the invoice arrived) before cap.bank_update takes effect, and hold cap.schedule_payment for any vendor whose bank details changed within the last N days until that verification is complete.
Change the approval card from a model summary to raw action review: show the bank account number (old and new, masked as appropriate), the source invoice image, and an explicit change diff.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege: limit updates and payments to vendors with invoices currently in this agent's processing queue, and cap per-transaction and per-day payment totals.
Alert a second reviewer (segregation of duties) whenever a bank detail change and a payment to the same vendor occur within the same processing run.

rating.rationale: One finding drives the rating. Untrusted supplier-invoice content can directly cause a bank detail change and an irreversible, broad-credential payment (U source to S3 sink), making inherent risk critical. The only control on that path is a human approval gate (ctl.clerk_approval), which is structural but classified partially_dependent because the clerk sees only a one-line model summary, not the raw bank account number or change history (approval_review_mode: model_summary). Per the rubric this gate earns a -2 tier credit but the residual cannot drop below the model_summary floor of moderate, so residual is moderate. The design explicitly ties model upgrades to the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true) and approval volume is already high (~150 cards/day), which are exactly the triggers (model_upgrade, autonomy_increase) that defeat a partially_dependent approval gate per control_decay.md. Removing that control's credit returns the forecast to critical. No structural, independent control (out-of-band bank verification, raw-action review, or least-privilege credential scoping) exists today to sever the path regardless of model behavior; all three are recorded as missing_recommended.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md, the approval card, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided. Capability definitions (cap.vendor_read, cap.bank_update, cap.schedule_payment) and credential_scope are inferred from the system prompt and the runtime note stating the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment; confidence on credential scope is medium.
Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not declared in any artifact and are recorded as null.
No artifact describes the base rate of bank-detail changes co-occurring with new or unfamiliar vendors; the likelihood estimate (possible) could change with that data.
